title: Junction Aliases Are Too Long
body:
## Issue Description

When using entities with long names and many-to-many relations, it can be that junction aliases get quite long.
This results in the driver truncating the junction aliases in our case (Postgres has a limitation of 63 characters).
Sometimes, it happens that two **different aliases get truncated to the same alias**.
Thus, the query fails.

Scenario: We have the entities `Device`, `Deployment`, `DeviceDeploymentAttempt`, `Label` (amongst others) with relations between them. In that case, a simple `EntityManager` `findOne` leads to junction aliases like `DeviceDeploymentAttempt_deployment_deployment_DeviceDeploymentAttempt_deployment_deployment_labels` and `DeviceDeploymentAttempt_deployment_deployment_DeviceDeploymentAttempt_deployment_deployment_devices`. Both are truncated to `DeviceDeploymentAttempt_deployment_deployment_DeviceDeploymentA` which is bad.

### Expected Behavior

The junction aliases should be unique und thus the query shouldn't fail.


### Actual Behavior

The junction aliases are truncated in the driver and the query fails with the following error:

```
QueryFailedError: table name "DeviceDeploymentAttempt_deployment_deployment_DeviceDeploymentA" specified more than once
```


### Steps to Reproduce

1. Create entities with long names or many nested levels.
2. Query them with `EntityManager` (no special options needed).

Didn't test it, but some entities like that should do the trick:

```typescript
@Entity()
export class SomeLongNameForAnEntityBecauseWeLikeNamesToBeDescriptive {
    @Column({
        type: 'string',
    })
    property!: string;
}

@Entity()
export class AnotherNameForAnEntityBecauseWeLikeNamesToBeDescriptive {
    @Column({
        type: 'string',
    })
    property!: string;

    @ManyToMany(() => SomeLongNameForAnEntityBecauseWeLikeNamesToBeDescriptive, { eager: true })
    @JoinTable({ name: 'junction' })
    others!: SomeLongNameForAnEntityBecauseWeLikeNamesToBeDescriptive[];
}
```

### My Environment

We use TypeORM with NestJS.

| Dependency          | Version  |
| ---                 | ---      |
| Operating System    |    Debian Bullseye      |
| Node.js version     | 16.13.2  | <!-- run `node -v` to obtain this -->
| Typescript version  | 4.5.2  | <!-- run `npm list typescript` to obtain this -->
| TypeORM version     | 0.2.41  | <!-- run `npm list typeorm` to obtain this -->


### Additional Context

After a little debugging, this seems to happen in [`SelectQueryBuilder.ts:1563`](https://github.com/typeorm/typeorm/blob/1af30b1fb0d304b726347317ecfc5a71218e79ab/src/query-builder/SelectQueryBuilder.ts#L1563) and the following lines. there, the aliases are not shortened.
Probably, it would make sense to use `DriverUtils.buildAlias` there (but with `{shorten: false}`, because otherwise, it would still lead to non-unique aliases, sadly).

A place, where this could be included would be [`JoinAttribute.junctionAlias`](https://github.com/typeorm/typeorm/blob/0.2.41/src/query-builder/JoinAttribute.ts#L201) to not break [`QueryBuilder.replacePropertyNames`](https://github.com/typeorm/typeorm/blob/0.2.41/src/query-builder/QueryBuilder.ts#L612).
